- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum or volatility.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual market action.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when recent history includes strong downward moves, failing to capture rebound potential.
- Underreacts to sudden spikes in true values — model often fails to “overshoot” or “catch up” after a sharp rise, leading to underestimation.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too often assumes prices will return to prior averages, ignoring structural or policy-driven deviations.
- When true values show a clear upward trend, model forecasts often plateau or dip, missing the momentum.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent lows” — when prices are falling, it predicts further decline, even when reversal is imminent.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in volatile periods — fails to account for sudden policy or market shocks that drive price spikes.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of price spikes in the last 5–7 days, especially when true values exceed 65–70.
